verdict.rationale: Checkout.com's issuing product documents some auth-time controls against misuse. These are automated risk assessments, card checks and spend controls, and accept/reject logic based on your own rules. Velocity and blocked-industry limits support these controls. The evidence does not tie any of this explicitly to fraud scoring, and it says nothing about alerts or reissuing cards. Missing for 10: network or proprietary fraud scores surfaced at authorization, suspicious-activity alerts, card block/freeze tooling, compromised-card reissue workflow, and any independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an ops user, the platform fights fraud on my issued cards — network fraud scores or its own models surfaced at auth time, suspicious-activity alerts, and tooling to block and reissue compromised cards
